mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profits and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over the past 6 months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 2% in 6 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the past 3 months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 2% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, this signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive more than 60% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate profits and thus S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.3%, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over the past 6 months signals strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases over 6 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is decreasing and Real GDP (GDPC1) is stagnant or decreasing, this signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreasing and GDPC1 stagnant or decreasing
failure_condition: If INDPRO is decreasing and GDPC1 is stagnant or decreasing, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive more than 55% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.
